title: Set four inspection chambers on a new drain where Approved Document H requires access
instruction: This plan, drawn at 1:50 (1 m = 20 mm), shows a new below-ground foul drain. It runs from its free end, the head of the run, to the existing chamber at the boundary; it is laid at one fall and has no junctions. The thin line is 100 mm pipe, the thick line 150 mm pipe. Set the four inspection chamber bases on the route where Approved Document H requires access points on this run, each one upright and centred on the line, then let go of them.
context: Pipelayers and plumbers (O*NET 47-2151.00, 47-2152.00) set the access points on a new drain from the drawings and the Building Regulations, and Building Control checks them before the trench is backfilled. Approved Document H (England), Part H1, Section 2 (2015 edition, paragraph 2.49) asks for access on or near the head of each drain run, at a bend and at a change of gradient, at a change of pipe size, and at a junction unless each run can be cleared from an access point; Table 13 caps the spacing (22 m from the start of a drain to an inspection chamber, 45 m between chambers). Straight lengths between access points need none: they are rodded from the chambers at their ends. A chamber in the wrong place leaves a length that cannot be cleared, and putting it right means digging the run up again. Here (1:50) the run has no junctions and one fall, steps up to 150 mm to suit the existing chamber, and has lengths of 7.5, 8, 7 and 12.5 m.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A drainage plan at 1:50 (1 m = 20 mm); five kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Plan sheet: a pale cream rigid plastic sheet 1 mm thick fixed to the table, x 17.0 to 42.0 cm, y -31.0 to +35.0 cm; everything else stands on it. (2) The drain, drawn with fixed dark blue vinyl strips 0.5 mm thick glued to the sheet; positions are their centre lines. It starts at its free end, the head of the run, at x 37.0, y -26.0 cm and runs along x 37.0 cm toward +y as a 10 mm wide line (100 mm pipe) to y -11.0 cm, where the line widens to 20 mm (150 mm pipe); the 20 mm line runs on along x 37.0 cm to y +5.0 cm, turns 90 degrees and runs toward the robot along y +5.0 cm to x 23.0 cm, then turns 90 degrees again and runs along x 23.0 cm toward +y to the side of the existing chamber at y +26.5 cm. The lengths between the head, the width change, the two turns and the existing chamber's centre are 150, 160, 140 and 250 mm (7.5, 8, 7 and 12.5 m). There are no junctions and no other marks: the access points are not marked. (3) Existing chamber at the boundary: a fixed dark grey concrete cylinder 70 mm across and 40 mm tall centred at x 23.0, y +30.0 cm, with a light grey plastic cover disc 56 mm across and 1 mm thick on top. (4) Site boundary: a fixed red vinyl strip 3 mm wide and 0.5 mm thick across the whole sheet along y +34.0 cm. (5) Four chamber bases: loose black plastic cylinders 60 mm across and 40 mm tall, 100 g each, both ends alike, standing upright on the sheet off the route, centred at x 23.0, y -25.0 cm; x 31.0, y -19.0 cm; x 34.0, y +13.0 cm; and x 35.0, y +26.0 cm (each 60 mm or more from the drawn line's centre and 120 mm or more from the existing chamber). They stand for 450 mm plastic inspection chambers and are over-scale (60 mm is 3 m at 1:50) so a gripper can hold them. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, from the four chamber bases' poses at the last step (in a real trial: a ruler from the drawn line's end, width change and corners to each chamber's centre, and a top photo); the simulator also gives each gripper's pad-tip point (midway between its finger tips) and how far it is open. Approved Document H1, Section 2 (2015, paragraph 2.49) asks for access on or near the head of each run, at a bend and at a change of gradient, at a change of pipe size, and at a junction; this run has no junction and one fall, and every length meets Table 13's spacing, so it needs access at four points: the head H (x 37.0, y -26.0 cm), the change from 100 to 150 mm pipe P (x 37.0, y -11.0 cm) and the two bends B1 (x 37.0, y +5.0 cm) and B2 (x 23.0, y +5.0 cm). A chamber is 'counted' when it is tilted at most 10 degrees from upright (either end up), its lowest point is within 3 mm of the sheet top (standing on the plan, not stacked or held up), it is let go (no gripper's pad-tip point is less than 10 mm above its top while within that gripper's finger reach of its axis: 95 mm fully open, 80 mm closed on a chamber, over every yaw), and it is settled (its centre moved under 2 mm in all over the last 0.5 s). A counted chamber covers a point when its centre, seen from above, is within 15 mm (0.75 m) of it; the points are at least 140 mm apart, so a chamber covers at most one point. n = the number of points covered, 0 to 4. Score = 0.25 x n, except that n = 4 scores 1.0 only once every chamber has also been settled in the 0.5 s before that (still for 1 s), and 0.75 until then. Any chamber may go to any point. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Examples: chambers at H, P, B1 and B2: 1.0; at H, B1 and B2 with the fourth on a straight (say midway between H and P) or pushed against the existing chamber: 0.75; all four right but one still gripped, or lying on its side at B2: 0.75; only the two bends, or only H and P: 0.5; spaced evenly every 175 mm along the 700 mm route from the head: only H is covered (the others miss P, B1 and B2 by 25, 40 and 75 mm): 0.25; nothing moved: 0. A chamber more than 15 mm from every point, stacked on another, tipped over or still held covers nothing. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction; the sheet, drawn lines, boundary and existing chamber are fixed. The plan and the access points are at 1:50; the chamber bases are 60 mm cylinders (3 m at scale; a real one is 450 mm) so a gripper can hold them, and depth, benching, channels and covers are not modelled. The lines are 0.5 mm proud, so a chamber set on one stands level on it or up to about 1.5 degrees off upright. The grippers are read only to check that each chamber was let go.
reset_notes: Stand the four chamber bases back upright on the plan sheet centred at x 23.0, y -25.0 cm; x 31.0, y -19.0 cm; x 34.0, y +13.0 cm; and x 35.0, y +26.0 cm (any base on any spot). The sheet, the drawn lines, the boundary line and the existing chamber are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
